shortDescription: By Emily Ou YongJapanese rubber futures eased on Thursday, pressured by lower oil prices, while a firmer yen added to the downside.($1 = 158.6400 yen)($1 = 6.7190 Chinese yuan)

children: Japanese rubber futures eased on Thursday, pressured by lower oil prices, while a firmer yen added to the downside.
The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for February delivery
was down 0.9 yen, or 0.21%, at 431.3 yen ($2.72) per kg as of 0113 GMT.
The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery
rose 120 yuan, or 0.64%, to 18,780 yuan ($2,795.06) per metric ton.
The most active October butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) gained 25 yuan, or 0.17%, to 15,055 yuan per metric ton.

The yen held its gains after a sudden, brief surge in the previous session that traders suspect may have been driven by government authorities, keeping pressure on the dollar ahead of a crucial U.S. jobs report.
A stronger currency makes yen-denominated assets less affordable to overseas buyers.
Oil prices edged lower as investors weighed the uncertainty of renewed military strikes between the U.S. and Iran that risk disrupting supplies from the Middle East.
Natural rubber often takes direction from oil prices as it competes for market share with synthetic rubber, which is made from crude oil.

The recent pullback reflects a correction of the weather-driven sentiment premium built up in the rally rather than a deterioration in fundamentals, with downstream demand unlikely to weaken substantially, said analysts from broker Tianfeng Futures in a note.
Natural rubber's failure to break above previous highs suggests the market may continue trading within a range for now, analysts from broker Gelin Dahua Futures said in a note.
The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for November delivery (STFX6) last traded at 233.5 U.S. cents per kg, up 0.7%.
